newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris drug-bust customs staff call protest strike.
newsitem.headline: Paris drug-bust customs staff call protest strike.

text.p: Paris customs officers said they would strike for three hours on Thursday to protest at staff shortages hampering them from controlling drug-smuggling from the Netherlands and other illegal trafficking.
The customs officers' union SNAD said on Wednesday the proposed stoppage would also oppose government plans to cut jobs in a budget austerity drive.
The union said the 10 officers in charge of controlling the French capital's railway stations could at best check one in every 15 trains coming into Paris daily on the Amsterdam-Brussels-Paris route.
"These trains are used by drug smugglers to carry their deadly goods...with virtual immunity," the union said in a statement.
The French government has often accused the Netherlands, whose narcotics laws are more permissive than other European Union countries, of failing to crack down on drugs smuggling.
Paris has delayed implementation of the Schengen accord to open land borders among seven EU countries, citing problems controlling drugs coming from the Netherlands.
